title: A. Fibonacciness
statement:
There is an array of 5 integers. Initially, you only know a_1,a_2,a_4,a_5. You may set a_3 to any positive integer, negative integer, or zero. The Fibonacciness of the array is the number of integers i (1 ≤ i ≤ 3) such that a_{i+2}=a_i+a_{i+1}. Find the maximum Fibonacciness over all integer values of a_3.

The first line contains an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 500) — the number of test cases.

The only line of each test case contains four integers a_1, a_2, a_4, a_5 (1 ≤ a_i ≤ 100).

For each test case, output the maximum Fibonacciness on a new line.

In the first test case, we can set a_3 to 2 to achieve the maximal Fibonacciness of 3.

In the third test case, it can be shown that 2 is the maximum Fibonacciness that can be achieved. This can be done by setting a_3 to 18.

Input:
```
61 1 3 51 3 2 18 10 28 100100 1 100 11 100 1 100100 100 100 100
```

Output:
```
3
2
2
1
1
2
```
